bible.tagline: A spider builds an early-warning station out of silk, takes her own scaffold down before dawn, and casts her shadow on every star the net catches.

decks.name: Orb Plate 1889
decks.world: An orb web built from nothing between two hedge stems before sunrise, drawn the way Henry McCook engraved it in 1889 and stamped the way a 1962 drawing office would stamp it: bone thread on slate, every radius numbered, a title block bottom-left that says DO NOT SCALE. The light is the grey half-hour before the sun finds the dew. The wonder is procedural: one animal, one line, forty minutes, a structure whose scaffold she eats as she lays the capture spiral and whose finished work she eats at dawn so the protein can be spun again. Register: Victorian plate engraving, drafting-office revision letters, specimen not taken.

BODY: silk is never white, it is the colour of plate paper; leaves Bloom headroom

decks.name: Sit and Wait
decks.world: A funnel web in long grass at three in the morning, seen from inside the funnel: the silk sheet is a drumskin and the spider is downstairs in the retreat, reading it through slits in her legs. A sodium streetlamp on a timer is the only light from above; nothing moves until something lands, and then bearing, amplitude, decision, rush. The dread is that stillness is the trap and she can wait twelve days; the wonder is that she tells wind from rain from prey by frequency alone. Register: 1970s nocturnal field biology, a seismograph pen on a paper drum, the darkest deck of the five.

BODY: a sheet web is dull grey, not silver; it must never glitter, so Bank B Bloom stays shut in this deck

moments: Sit in Twelve Days with only the row-1 BED and row-2 BODY pads lit and the SCOPE as the single moving thing for longer than feels safe, then fire Scene Launch 3 on a kick and let Line Scape Wobble on the highs say that something landed.

On Pluck the Line, tap the row-4 Stroboscope pad by hand in a two-then-pause rhythm; the strobe is never clocked and never on the FFT, your finger is the spider's foreleg; at The Rush slam the Bank C knob (Displace) to full on the drop, press Fragment in Bank D once and let go, and pull Bank C back to zero within two bars so the sheet collapses and re-forms.

The Husk: toggle Freeze in Bank D, then pull every layer fader except TEXT, GRAIN and SCOPE to zero; the room is left with one red word, static and the trace, and you stay there longer than the room expects.

decks.name: Arachne's Loom
decks.world: Two weavers who became the stories they told, shown at closing time in a museum: Arachne, Idmon's daughter of Lydia, who wove the gods' crimes without a flaw and was struck with the shuttle, hanged, and told to live; and Kwaku Ananse, who paid the sky god Nyame four captures for every story in the world and keeps them in his web. The light is gallery halogen on bronze and gilt thread on wine-dark warp, with the title card of a BBC Schools 'Myth and Legend' broadcast on 16mm. The dread is the verdict, one madder strobe and a torn cloth; the wonder is the cosmogram, a Rings web whose nodes are stories and whose sweep lights them one at a time. Everything is weave: Checkered is warp and weft, the Pattern Maker is the tapestry, the spider is the shape left when the woman is subtracted, and the tab switch into this deck is a change of century.

decks.name: Goose Summer
decks.world: Inside the egg sac is the quietest room in the world: three hundred eggs in wound silk, lit through from outside like a lamp through linen, with the mother on the outside not eating and not leaving, and in some species the first meal. Then the moult, where a spider leaves an exact ghost of herself and walks out soft; then the spiderlings on tiptoe at the top of a fence post, abdomens to the wind, throwing a line into the sky's electric field and letting go. Darwin found the Beagle's rigging coated in their silk sixty miles from land, and Middle English called the stuff gossamer, goose summer. The light is milk and amber on the only light ground in the instrument, 16mm natural history circa 1979, microscope-close and heavy with grain; the register is a naturalist's tenderness in lower case, and this is the deck you switch to when the room needs to breathe.

decks.name: Dew Line Station
decks.world: A Cold War early-warning radar station whose antenna sweep leaves an orb web as its trace: the DEW Line of 1957 and dew on a web at dawn are the same picture, a net strung across the dark that catches light so you can see what is coming. The dome is a telescope too, and every telescope already contains a spider: the four vanes that hold the secondary mirror cast a cross on every bright star, and surveyors once strung their reticles with a single strand of silk. Louise Bourgeois' Maman stands over the dance floor, nine metres of steel seen from underneath with marble eggs held in the sac; Arabella spun in Skylab in 1973; CP1919 ticks every 1.337 seconds and was not a signal, it was a clock. The light is P7 phosphor, signal white and tape-reel amber on blue-black, 1981 regional continuity with no warmth at all, and the deck ends in a legitimate black, a test card, and a stop.

bible.fft_philosophy: Lows (kick, 40-120 Hz) drive structural tension only - Suckr strength, Rings Size and Spacing contracting a few percent, Trails length, Sine Wave Modulation Depth - through an envelope follower with fast attack and a 300-600 ms release, so the web tightens on the kick and relaxes between hits like a load on a structure rather than a flash. Mids (200 Hz-2 kHz) drive the slow motion rates (Spiral Speed, Line Scape Wobble, Abstract Field drift, Metaballs Speed) so a busy mix makes the world breathe faster but never flicker, and highs (6 kHz up) drive the silk alone - Fuzzyness, Displace amount, Bloom and dew brightness - in ranges small enough that silk shivers and never tears. Nothing ever reacts on TEXT (words must be readable on a wall at 2am), nothing moves the FIGURE's position (the spider decides where she is), hue never reacts anywhere, nothing on AURA reacts, column transitions never react, the rotation of any orb never reacts (a web does not spin to a beat), the Radar sweep period never reacts because it is the clock, and strobe frequency is not a signal path at all - every flash is a Stroboscope pad under a finger. The SCOPE layer alone takes the raw unsmoothed spectrum, precisely so that everything else can afford to be slow. Reactivity is a musician's hand on a fader, not a VU meter: smoothed, thresholded, and deliberately missing the obvious beat half the time.
bible.wildcard_rationale: The single most unexpected idea is that the web is never drawn, only revealed: the stock Radar effect in Bank A is the spider. Every ring, radius and spiral already exists on its layer, but the composition only shows what the beam has passed over, so the performer builds the orb by letting the sweep rotate while mashing structural pads, and a new ring lands exactly where the beam is. Lock that sweep to eight beats and it becomes the eight-legged clock: one revolution is one bar, each leg is a beat, and the whole composition keeps time visibly without a single frame of media, which is also why the pack is called Dew Line - the 1957 Distant Early Warning radar line and dew on an orb web at dawn are the same picture, a net strung across the dark that catches light so you can see what is coming, which is exactly what a club wall is for. Two smaller wildcards now live inside that one. In Orb Plate 1889, columns five and six are formwork removal: the same Spiral generator with Direction reversed, Spread tightened and Trails up, so the audience watches the dense capture spiral eat the dry scaffold from rim to hub while the title block stamps SCAFFOLD REMOVED, the one gesture that proves the spider is a builder and not a decoration, because she makes a temporary structure, uses it, and takes it down. In Dew Line Station, column six takes the telescope spider literally: the four vanes that hold every reflector's secondary mirror are called the spider by every astronomer who has collimated one, and the cross on every bright star is her shadow, so opening Bloom and Sparkles makes every dew return and marble egg grow a four-armed cross. Read in one breath, the bible says the spider builds a temporary structure, takes it down, and casts her shadow on every star the net catches.

decks.name: Orb Protocol
decks.world: The web as tensile architecture, drawn on a drafting table in 1962: white ink on Prussian blueprint, Frei Otto's soap-film models pinned to the wall, and the orb-weaver's build order typed up as a specification with revision letters. Light is a cold north window and one ultraviolet lamp on vellum; the silk fluoresces, the paper does not. The wonder is that the geometry is exact and nobody commissioned it; the dread is that it is eaten at dawn and rebuilt, so the drawing is always Rev C. Register: engineering drawing - section lines, dimension ticks, title block, DO NOT SCALE.

decks.name: Funnel Watch
decks.world: A sheet web at the mouth of a funnel in long grass at three in the morning, under a sodium streetlamp on a timer; the spider is downstairs in the retreat and listens with her feet. Light is sodium amber from above, infrared false colour where something warm walks, and strip-chart phosphor green for the record. The dread is that stillness is the trap and the strike takes two hundred milliseconds; the wonder is that she can tell wind from rain from prey by frequency alone. Register: 1970s nocturnal field biology, night-vision scope, seismograph pen on a paper drum.

Light is gallery halogen on terracotta and bronze, gold leaf picking up the last of it. The wonder is that all the stories in the world were once in a gourd the spider bought from the sky god; the dread is the punishment for weaving better than a goddess. Register: catalogue labels, black-figure ware, warp stripes, the loom as the first computer.

decks.name: Silk Nursery

Light is milk glass and amber lantern on the only white ground in the instrument; the wonder is the ballooning, the dread is that in some species the mother is the first meal. Register: 1950s natural-history film stock, incubator telemetry, nursery wallpaper, Bourgeois' marble eggs under the bronze.

decks.name: Phosphor Web
decks.world: 1981: a regional continuity suite and a coastal early-warning radar station share one green phosphor, and the web is read as an antenna array by an operator with eight hands. Every sweep of the scope lays another radius; every tremor on a thread is a contact at a bearing; the clock on the wall has eight hands and no face. Light is P1 phosphor on black, ident white, tape-reel amber, and it holds for three seconds after the source is gone, which is the dread: the signal arrives before the thing that made it. Register: BBC Radiophonic, test card, teletext, PPI scope, closedown.

proposals.fft_philosophy: Sub and kick (20-120 Hz) drive TENSION only: Suckr strength, Rings Size, Spiral Zoom, so the web tightens toward the hub on the beat and relaxes between, a load on a structure rather than a flash. Low-mids (120-500 Hz) are smoothed over about two seconds and breathe the BED (Gradient position, Abstract Field Amplitude, Line Scape Height) so the environment swells with the track's body, never its transients. The snare and mid band (1-4 kHz) is gated to a one-shot that may touch LIGHT layer opacity and Stroboscope frequency once and decay fast, because a strike happens once. Highs (6-16 kHz) drive SHIVER only: Fuzzyness, Displace amount, Sine Wave Modulation Depth, Line Scape Wobble, with a hard ceiling so silk trembles but never tears. Never reactive: text position, size and opacity (typography is the point of view and does not dance), rotation of any orb (a web does not spin to a beat), hue and palette, master opacity and column transitions, and anything on the AURA layer; the SCOPE layer is the one place the music is allowed to be literal, and it is the only one.
proposals.wildcard_rationale: The most unexpected idea is that one scene exists to destroy the previous one. A real orb-weaver lays the auxiliary spiral first, from the hub outward, as a non-sticky scaffold she can walk on; then she lays the capture spiral from the outside in and cuts the auxiliary away as she goes, eating it. So in Orb Protocol, column 6 (Capture Spiral) is built as the formal negation of column 5 (Aux Spiral): the same Spiral generator with Direction reversed and Spread tightened, a long column transition, and Trails in the bank so the audience watches the sparse spiral being consumed by the dense one from the rim toward the hub, and the TEXT layer stamps SCAFFOLD REMOVED. A VJ journey normally accumulates; this one includes formwork removal, which is what a structural engineer does on every real build and what every orb-weaver does every night. It belongs because it is the single clearest proof that the spider is a builder and not a decoration: she makes a temporary structure, uses it, and takes it down, and an instrument that claims she is a geometer has to be honest enough to do the same.

proposals.tagline: A spider builds an early-warning radar station out of silk, and the whole room is caught in the net that catches light.

decks.name: Radial Survey
decks.world: The orb web as an engineering drawing being plotted in real time: bridge line, frame, radii, hub, auxiliary spiral, capture spiral, in the order a real Araneus lays them. The light is bone-white silk on drafting-paper black with a single phosphor-teal plotter glow, like a 1981 Open University maths module shot on a vector terminal. The wonder is procedural: nothing is drawn until the stage before it holds, and the whole web arrives over eight bars with the certainty of a theodolite. The spider is the draughtsman and the survey mark at once; she does not measure, she simply knows.

Everything is weave: Checkered is warp and weft, the Pattern Maker is the tapestry, and the spider is the shape left when the woman is subtracted.

decks.name: Dew Line Station
decks.world: A Cold War early-warning radar station where the antenna's sweep leaves an orb web as its trace: the DEW Line of 1957 and dew on a web at dawn are the same picture, a net that catches light to see what is coming. proposals.fft_philosophy: Lows (kick, 40-120 Hz) drive structural tension only: Rings Size and Spacing contract a few percent, Displace and Goo amount, Trails length, Sine Wave Modulation Depth, all through an envelope follower with fast attack and a 300-600 ms release so the web tightens on the kick and relaxes between hits rather than jumping. Mids (200 Hz-2 kHz) drive motion rates: Spiral Speed, Line Scape Wobble, Abstract Field drift, the slow things, scaled so a busy mix makes the world breathe faster but never flicker. Highs (6 kHz up) drive the silk: Fuzzyness, Bloom amount, Metaballs dew brightness and the Strobe gate, which opens only above a threshold so hi-hats shimmer the threads and only a real crash fires a flash. Nothing ever reacts in the TEXT layer (words must be readable at 2am on a wall), nothing moves the FIGURE's position (the spider decides where she is, not the kick), hue never reacts anywhere, the Radar sweep period never reacts (it is the clock), and the SCOPE's scale is fixed so the readout stays a readout. Reactivity is a musician's hand on a fader, not a VU meter: smoothed, thresholded, and deliberately missing the obvious beat half the time.
proposals.wildcard_rationale: The single most unexpected idea is that the web is never drawn, only revealed: the stock Radar effect in Bank A is the spider. Every ring, radius and spiral already exists on its layer, but the composition only shows what the beam has passed over, so the performer builds the orb web by letting the sweep rotate while mashing structural pads, and a new ring lands exactly where the beam is. Lock that sweep to eight beats and it becomes the eight-legged clock: one revolution is one bar, each leg is a beat, and the whole composition keeps time visibly without a single frame of media. That is also why the pack is called Dew Line: the 1957 Distant Early Warning radar line and dew on an orb web at dawn are the same picture, a net strung across the dark that catches light so you can see what is coming, which is exactly what a club wall is for. It belongs because it turns an effect the performer already owns into a point of view, and it gives the five decks one shared gesture, the sweep, that reads on a big LED wall at 2am with bass whether the music is techno or ambient.

proposals.tagline: A spider is an engineer who draws with one line, and this instrument puts the other end of that line in your hand.

decks.name: The Spinningwork
decks.world: An orb web being built from nothing between two hedge stems before sunrise, drawn the way Henry McCook drew it in 1889: a plate engraving, bone thread on slate, every radius numbered. The light is the grey half-hour before the sun finds the dew. The wonder is procedural: one animal, one line, forty minutes, a structure that is torn down and eaten every dawn so the protein can be spun again. Register: Victorian field notebook, specimen not taken.

decks.name: Sit and Wait
decks.world: A funnel web in long grass at night, seen from inside the funnel: the silk sheet is a drumskin and the spider reads it through slits in her legs. Nothing moves until something lands; then bearing, amplitude, decision, rush. The light is a single strike of white and then the sheet going still again. Register: a seismograph log kept by a predator who can wait twelve days.

decks.name: Loom and Mirror
decks.world: A Lydian loom, a goddess with a shuttle, a rope, and a girl who will hang by a thread forever because she wove the truth about the gods. Then the mirror in the tower at Shalott, where the web flies out and the glass cracks, and finally the sky god's price, paid by Kwaku Ananse so that every story would be called a spider story. Tapestry light: gilt thread on wine-dark warp, a candle in a mirror. Register: Ovid, Tennyson and an Akan night-telling, all in capitals.

decks.name: Goose Summer
decks.world: Under the belly of Louise Bourgeois' bronze Maman, looking up into a sac of marble eggs; then the real sac, the three hundred that hatch, huddle, moult, and stand on tiptoe with their abdomens to the wind until a strand lifts them. Darwin found the Beagle's rigging coated in their silk sixty miles from land. The light is low sun on gossamer, which Middle English called goose summer. Register: a naturalist's tenderness and a sculptor's grief, in lower case.

decks.name: Spider Line
decks.world: A phosphor radar scope where each sweep pins one more radius until an orb is on the screen; a telescope whose secondary mirror hangs on four vanes that astronomers call the spider, so every bright star wears her cross-shaped shadow; Skylab, 1973, where Arabella spun the first web in orbit. Surveyors once made crosshairs from a single strand of silk. Green and amber on black, 1981 Radiophonic, a log read aloud by a terminal. The dread is the carrier going quiet; the wonder is that silk was always a signal line.

proposals.fft_philosophy: Sub and kick (roughly 40-120 Hz) drive tension, never luminance: Rings Size contracts three to five percent, Line Width thickens, Line Scape Height drops, with a fast attack and a slow release so the web tightens on the kick and relaxes over the bar. Low-mids (120-600 Hz) drive slow structural motion only: Rotation and Spiral Speed, Metaballs Speed, the drift of the figure. Highs above 4 kHz drive shiver: Fuzzyness, Wobble, dew jitter, Text Glow In, all in small ranges so silk trembles and never flails. Nothing in the composition may pump opacity like a VU meter, and these must never react at all: any text position, size or content; the bed layer; strobe frequency, which is hand-played; hue; scene or column changes. The SCOPE layer alone takes the raw unsmoothed spectrum, precisely so that everything else can afford to be slow.
proposals.wildcard_rationale: The most unexpected idea here is that the telescope already contains a spider: the four thin vanes that hold a reflector's secondary mirror are called the spider by every astronomer who has ever collimated one, and the cross-shaped diffraction spikes on every bright star in every astrophotograph are literally her shadow cast on the light. Deck five's Four Vanes scene takes that fact at face value, so that when the performer opens Bloom every point of light on the screen grows a cross, and the silk-crosshair column before it (surveyors and astronomers once strung their reticles with a single strand of spider silk because nothing drawn by hand was fine enough) makes the lineage explicit. It belongs because it is the thesis of the whole bible, not a decoration on it: the spider is the engineer of the net that catches light, and the pack moves from the hedge at dawn through the hunt, the loom and the nursery to arrive at a radar scope and a star, where the same geometry that catches a fly turns out to be the thing that lets us see. Arabella spinning in Skylab in 1973 is the runner-up, and she is in the same deck for the same reason.
